chapters.title: 01 / Operational overview
chapters.caption: FloodGuard AI: an actual browser walkthrough. Models are assumed trained on small datasets; all demonstrated readings are illustrative.

chapters.title: 02 / Command statistics
chapters.caption: National screening summarizes district risk, priorities, and monitoring intervals in one command view.

chapters.title: 02 / Command statistics
chapters.caption: The river summary compares city discharge and forecast values, with timestamps and a manual refresh control.

chapters.title: 02 / Command statistics
chapters.caption: The rainfall table compares current, recent, and forecast rainfall across the four operational cities.

chapters.title: 02 / Command statistics
chapters.caption: System information shows the configured data mode, monitoring interval, and active risk engine.

chapters.title: 03 / National GIS layers
chapters.caption: Toggle district boundaries, screening, waterways, catchments, and monitoring categories on the interactive map.

chapters.title: 03 / Reference outlines and Flood Hub integration
chapters.caption: Compare the available Kashmir outlines and enable Flood Hub markers. The gauges shown here are illustrative integration examples.

chapters.title: 04 / Coordinate lookup
chapters.caption: Enter latitude and longitude to inspect local coverage. The selected coordinate is pinned on the map.

chapters.title: 05 / Catchment study mode
chapters.caption: Enable corresponding layers to focus on the selected district and hydrological sub-basin, including matching river features.

chapters.title: 06 / Station hover cards
chapters.caption: Hover and pin a priority monitoring station to inspect readings, provenance, and stored trends.

chapters.title: 07 / Station discharge forecast
chapters.caption: Station details link to an interactive forecast, separate historical series, date inspection, a readings table, and CSV download.

chapters.title: 08 / Glaciers and headwaters
chapters.caption: Inspect glacier coverage and upstream drainage, including glaciers that contribute to Pakistan's river basins.

chapters.title: 09 / Satellite water extent
chapters.caption: Select a place to display a dated satellite water-mask overlay. This recording uses an illustrative U-Net output.

chapters.title: 10 / Rainfall heatmap
chapters.caption: Switch between observed accumulation windows and 24-hour or 72-hour forecasts. Colors follow the rainfall scale.

chapters.title: 11 / Population exposure analysis
chapters.caption: GIS Operations estimates exposed people and mapped settlements, with district or tehsil breakdowns and coverage information.

chapters.title: 12 / Exposure controls and map overlays
chapters.caption: The analysis supports historical water, configured segmentation, uploaded polygons, and synthetic scenarios; inspect the existing result and its layers.

chapters.title: 13 / Predictive model views
chapters.caption: Five predictive views cover riverine, flash, urban, seasonal basin, and upstream or transboundary risk, with forecast times and target selectors.

chapters.title: 14 / Riverine short-term model
chapters.caption: Riverine forecasts: XGBoost baseline inputs, Trimmu and Balloki targets, discharge forecasts, and flood classes over 24–48 hours.

chapters.title: 14 / Flash-flood model
chapters.caption: Flash-flood guidance combines rainfall, soil moisture, and GIS features for catchment risk within six hours.

chapters.title: 14 / Urban flooding model
chapters.caption: Urban susceptibility uses city-scale targets, rainfall, drainage context, and selectable forecast intervals.

chapters.title: 14 / Seasonal basin model
chapters.caption: Seasonal basin risk shows forecasts over weeks to months, with target-specific risk series.

chapters.title: 14 / Upstream anomaly model
chapters.caption: Upstream and transboundary risk highlights anomalous flow changes over hours to days. Model outputs are illustrative in this demo.

chapters.title: 15 / Upstream source flood watch
chapters.caption: Select upper-basin stations, compare GloFAS and GEOGloWS series, and inspect historical trends, rainfall, and forecast risk signals.

chapters.title: 16 / Source forecast context
chapters.caption: Each station includes provider summaries, expected peaks, rainfall context, location details, and scheduled or manual refresh.

chapters.title: 17 / River monitoring table
chapters.caption: Filter monitoring stations by river or name, switch units, and compare current flow, forecasts, flood categories, and expected peaks.

chapters.title: 18 / Station network and chart
chapters.caption: Open a station to inspect its upstream network and forecast. Chart legends and date inspection help distinguish the displayed series.

chapters.title: 19 / Citizen reports
chapters.caption: Citizen reports provide a scrollable database-backed feed, coordinates, optional image or video links, priority flags, and closure status.

chapters.title: 20 / Submit a geolocated report
chapters.caption: Create a report using coordinates, browser location, or a Google Maps link. Image GPS fields remain visible when no geotag is available.

chapters.title: 21 / Prioritize and close reports
chapters.caption: Flag a report for attention, then close it in the database. New reports appear in the active window before remaining in the saved feed.

chapters.title: 22 / Monitoring simulation
chapters.caption: Configure a station, measurement, units, test thresholds, and a reading profile to exercise the monitoring workflow.

chapters.title: 23 / Threshold crossing and saved results
chapters.caption: Play the test scenario. Threshold crossings save simulated readings and create linked alerts and incidents.

chapters.title: 24 / Alert review
chapters.caption: Review threshold alerts, distinguish operational and simulated flows, and open the linked incident.

chapters.title: 25 / Incident management
chapters.caption: The incident view records severity, status, location, and timestamps. Linked details preserve the simulated-flow context.

chapters.title: 26 / System activity
chapters.caption: The activity timeline records model decisions, monitoring changes, report actions, and simulated response events.

chapters.title: 27 / Command overview
chapters.caption: The walkthrough covers the portal as it runs in a web browser. Small-dataset training is an assumption; this video does not validate model accuracy.
